<!-- issue-warning -->
> [!WARNING]
> Before submitting a PR, please make sure that:
> - A maintainer has triaged this issue and applied the `ready` label
> - This issue has no assignee
> - No duplicate PR exists
>
> PRs not meeting these requirements may be automatically closed.

### MLflow version

3.15.1 (official `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.15.1-full` image).

The issue and diagnostic patch were reproduced on this version. Newer releases have not been runtime-tested for this report.

### System information

- **OS Platform and Distribution (e.g., Linux Ubuntu 16.04)**: Linux ARM64 container; original deployment on AWS ECS Fargate, standalone reproduction using Docker on macOS.
- **Python version**: 3.10.18 in the official container (server and reproduction script).
- **Browser**: Chrome 153 on macOS for the standalone reproduction.
- **Backend store**: PostgreSQL in the original deployment; SQLite in the standalone reproduction.
- **UI**: Packaged UI, not a development server.

### Describe the problem

When different assessment names occur on different batches of traces within one run, the run's **Traces** tab only discovers assessment columns present in the first 100 traces. Assessment names that occur exclusively on later pages are absent from both the table and **Columns → Assessments**.

Loading every trace by scrolling does not fix the column selector. This makes it impossible to select the missing assessment column through that selector, despite its results being stored successfully.

**Expected:** All assessment names belonging to the selected run are available as columns, independently of trace pagination. A trace need not have a value for every assessment.

**Actual:** With 220 traces split between `judge_a` and `judge_b`, the first page contains only `judge_b`, so the UI shows **Assessments (1/1)**. After loading **220 of 220** traces, it still shows **1/1**, and the column selector still offers only `judge_b`.

The same behavior was originally observed with three assessment names and 340 traces. All three aggregate run metrics were present, but only one assessment column was available.

#### Findings

In [`useMlflowTraces.tsx` at v3.15.1](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/v3.15.1/mlflow/server/js/src/shared/web-shared/genai-traces-table/hooks/useMlflowTraces.tsx):

Relates to #26225 and [RFC-0014 (job executor remote plugins)](https://github.com/mlflow/rfcs/blob/main/rfcs/0014-job-executor-remote-plugins/0014-job-executor-remote-plugins.md)

### What changes are proposed in this pull request?

#26225 confined custom `@scorer` code execution to the job executor process. This PR adds an **experimental `docker` job executor backend**, so that on-demand custom scorer runs can run in a hardened container instead of on the server host.

**Per-job backend dispatch.** The executor engine (`MLFLOW_SERVER_JOB_EXECUTION_ENGINE=executor`) now runs each job on the backend recorded on its job row.
- The runner starts every configured backend: `MLFLOW_JOB_DEFAULT_EXECUTOR_BACKEND`, plus `MLFLOW_JOB_CUSTOM_SCORER_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` when it is different.
- Cancel and startup recovery go to each job's own backend.
- A job whose backend is not served fails closed.
- The old submit-time rule that the two settings must be equal is removed. Instead, setting a custom scorer backend other than `local` without the executor engine now refuses to start the server, even when the default backend names the same backend, so custom scorers cannot silently run somewhere else.

**Routing.** `AbstractJobExecutor.supports_job(job_name, params)` has a default of `True`. A custom scorer job that the custom scorer backend does not support stays on the default backend, and the router logs it.

**`DockerJobExecutor`** (`mlflow/server/jobs/docker_executor.py`). Job containers have no network, so they cannot reach the server either. Data moves through bind-mounted files:
1. On the host, the job's planner fetches the traces into a read-only input mount.
2. The container runs only the scorer (`_score_traces_from_file`) and writes its result to an output mount.
3. The host treats that output as untrusted:
   - It opens the result with `O_NOFOLLOW`, rejects anything that is not a regular file, caps the read at 8 MiB (which also bounds the memory the host uses to parse it), and type-checks every field.

The pull change itself is about 1,300 lines in these commits: `Implement verified, all-or-nothing Skill pull for the SDK and CLI`, `Address self-review findings on Skill pull`, and `Tidy Skill pull code and tests`.

RFC: [Pull semantics](https://github.com/mlflow/rfcs/blob/main/rfcs/0008-mvp-skill-registry/0008-mvp-skill-registry.md#pull-semantics), [Pull details](https://github.com/mlflow/rfcs/blob/main/rfcs/0008-mvp-skill-registry/implementation-details.md#pull-semantics-details)

### What changes are proposed in this pull request?

Standalone Skill pull for the SDK and the CLI. Agent Plugin pull is deferred.

**Shared client logic** (`mlflow/genai/skill_content/pull.py`)
- `resolve_skill_version(uri)` resolves a `skills:/` URI through registry metadata:
  - `skills:/name/3` gets an exact version.
  - `skills:/name@alias` follows an alias.
  - `skills:/name` resolves the dynamic latest version on every call.
  - `skills:/@org/...` sets the organization.
- `pull_skill_version(version, destination)` fetches the version's persisted source through the shared fetchers (`fetch_source`):
  - Git, OCI, and ZIP use their typed sources.
  - `mlflow` uses the artifact tree plus the persisted subpath.
  - Plugin membership is never consulted, and the server never transfers content.
- Hardening:
  - Registry metadata can never make a pull read the caller's filesystem: a Git or MLflow source whose value is a local path is refused.
  - A version whose metadata is `deleted` is refused before anything is fetched.
- Destination rules:
  - Allowed: a destination that doesn't exist, or an existing empty directory.

- Staging and verification:
  - Content is staged in a hidden sibling directory, falling back to the system temp dir when the parent can't be written to.
  - `fetch_source` rejects symlinks, hard links, and special files for every source type.

### What changes are proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds four **user-journey tests** for the Skill Registry, in one new file: `tests/server/skill_registry/test_user_journeys.py`. No production code changes.

A user-journey test uses the registry the way a person would: several API calls in a row against a real, running MLflow server, checking that what one step did is what the next step sees.
